body.statement: Under the premises of \(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\), suppose every entry of the rational input \(\mathcal O_G\) has binary encoding length at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\). The fraction-free immutable-row implementation of \(\operatorname{Enum}_G\), including common-ancestry computation, has deterministic total bit-operation time and bit storage polynomial in \(p\), \(m\), \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\), \(2^p\), \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\), and the total emitted encoding length. Canonically reduced determinant-ratio certificates decide equality of interned rows. Thus no superpolynomial intermediate or certificate growth is forced in this rational published-class regime.
body.proof_tex:
Write every rational input coordinate in lowest terms with positive denominator.  For one principal regression solve, multiply its coefficient matrix and right-hand side by the product \(d\) of the denominators of the at most \((p+1)^2\) entries in the augmented matrix.  If each numerator and denominator has at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\) binary digits, then
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(d)\le(p+1)^2L_{\mathrm{bits}},
 \qquad \operatorname{bits}(dx)=O(p^2L_{\mathrm{bits}}).
 \tag{18}
\]
This common positive scaling leaves the solution unchanged.  The principal within-view covariance matrix is positive definite by \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\); hence its leading principal minors, after fixing any ordering of \(A\), are positive and fraction-free elimination needs no pivot.

By \(\texttt{lem:bareiss-minor-growth}\), every division is exact and every transformed coefficient is a signed bordered minor.  If a \(k\times k\) integer matrix \(K\) has entries of magnitude below \(2^h\), the Leibniz formula gives
\[
 |\det K|\le k!2^{kh},
\]
and therefore, using (18) and \(k\le p+1\),
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(\det K)
 =O(p^3L_{\mathrm{bits}}+p\log p).
 \tag{19}
\]
The adjugate identity expresses every regression coordinate as a bordered-minor numerator divided by the nonzero principal determinant.  Greatest-common-divisor reduction with a positive denominator produces a canonical certificate of the height in (19).  Two rational coordinates, rows, or decoded tuples are equal exactly when their canonical certificates agree.

The ordered exact-real algorithm in \(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\) uses polynomially many operations in \(p\), \(m\), \(2^p\), and \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\).  Equations (18)--(19) show that each rational field or comparison operation has polynomial-height operands.  Ordinary integer arithmetic is polynomial in their bit length.  Euclid's algorithm is polynomial as well: after at most two remainder steps its positive second operand is less than half its previous value, so \(h\)-bit inputs require at most \(2h+1\) remainder steps on at most \(h\)-bit operands.  Fragment keys contain \(p\) identifiers of \(O(p)\) bits and create no rational-expression growth.  Published common ancestry is the empty relation by \(\texttt{prop:published-common-union-support-ancestry-empty}\), so its exact output costs \(O(1)\).

Multiplying the polynomial operation count by the polynomial per-operation bit cost, then adding the total emitted encoding length, proves the time assertion.  Multiplying (19) by the stored row and output counts and adding the tries proves the storage assertion.  Each row is solved directly from an original principal covariance system, so the height bound is not recursively iterated through \(2^p\) states.
body.justification: The published exact-real algorithm retains its deterministic rational output-polynomial implementation.
body.gap: Unit-cost exact-real accounting alone does not control certificate height.
body.consumer: Exact symbolic implementations of the all-orders boundary have a Turing-model guarantee.
